title: How a House Gets Built, Step by Step
excerpt: From site clearing to handover: the usual order of work on a new home.
content:
Every build is different, but most follow the same sequence.

## 1. Plan and approve
Design, drawings, budget and permits come first. Changes are cheap on paper and expensive on site.

## 2. Prepare the site
Clear, level and mark out the plot, and organise drainage, access and temporary services.

## 3. Foundations and structure
Excavate, pour foundations and let them cure, then raise the walls and frame.

## 4. Roof and weather-tightness
Once the roof is on and openings are closed, the interior can be worked on regardless of weather.

## 5. Services and finishes
Electrics, plumbing, plaster, floors and paint, followed by inspections and handover.

Allow time between stages: concrete needs days to cure, and plaster needs to dry before painting.

*This article is general information for planning and learning. Building rules, permits and safety requirements differ by location. Always follow your local codes and consult a qualified engineer, architect or licensed contractor before you build.*

title: Concrete Basics for Homeowners
excerpt: Why strength comes from the right mix, careful pouring and patient curing.
content:
Concrete is cement, sand, stone and water, and each part matters.

## The mix
Too much water makes concrete easier to pour but weaker. Follow the mix specified by your engineer.

## Pouring
Place it in layers, compact it to remove air pockets and keep it level.

## Curing
Concrete gains strength as it cures, not as it dries. Keep it damp and shaded for several days.

## Reinforcement
Steel bars carry the pulling forces concrete cannot. Keep them clean and covered by the specified thickness of concrete.

title: Site Safety Fundamentals
excerpt: The habits that prevent most building-site accidents.
content:
Most site accidents are preventable.

## Wear the basics
- hard hat
- safety boots
- gloves and eye protection
- hearing protection near loud tools

## Work at height
Scaffolding needs a firm base, guardrails and regular inspection. Never overload platforms.

## Keep the site tidy
Clear walkways, store materials safely and cover openings.

## Talk about it
A short briefing each morning about the day's hazards is one of the cheapest safety measures there is.

title: Keeping Water Out: A Waterproofing Guide
excerpt: Where leaks start and how to stop them early.
content:
Water is the most common cause of building damage.

## Know the weak points
Roofs, bathrooms, balconies, basements and joints between materials.

## Choose a system
Membranes, coatings and cement-based products each suit different places. Follow the manufacturer's instructions on surface preparation.

## Test before you finish
Flood-test bathroom floors and flat roofs before tiling or covering them.

## Maintain
Clean gutters and drains, and inspect sealants yearly.
